summary: Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009), studying under MA supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD from the University of Würzburg (1874–1879) and studied under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, the State Museum, Lucknow, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Alois Müller was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He held posts at the Vienna University Library (~1869–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and Graz University Library (Direktor, 1879).

Aloysius Pieris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned degrees including a PhD from the University of Sri Lanka and a Th.D. from Tilburg University, and he founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre from 1974.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Yasuaki Nara.

Alvappillai Veluppillai was an Indologist and linguist who studied under K. Kanapathypillai at the University of Ceylon and Thomas Burrow at the University of Oxford. His career included posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Jaffna, Uppsala University, and Arizona State University.

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1947–1948). He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968), as a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, and as a UNESCO adviser.
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

Amanda Goodman is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching post at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under A. K. Warder (attested 1984) and studied with Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, Masafumi Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali is an Indologist and linguist who has served as a Lecturer in Urdu at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held positions at Jadavpur University, the University of Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard University.
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Hyderabad (ending 2009) and later served there as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Mary Margaret McCabe, Verity Harte, and others. She has held posts at the University of York, University of St Andrews, and Yale-NUS College.
Amdo Zen Karwa Chökyi Sengé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Amelia Bonea is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Heidelberg University (~2005–2009). She became Senior Lecturer in Global History of Science, Technology and Medicine at the University of Manchester (~2018).

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (ending 2012). She held posts at Naropa University and Central Michigan University (both attested 2019).

Amin Sweeney was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London (~1967–1970). He held posts at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and the University of California, Berkeley (1986–1991, 1998).
